author: The Entertainment Oracle
title: 2017 was another big year for streaming services, as more a
text:
2017 was another big year for streaming services, as more and more entered the space dominated by the likes of Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) and Hulu. Granted, that’s not a bad thing if one of those niche services is in your wheelhouse, but as the media seems laser-focused on the big three (soon to be four), so should investors.
As we get deeper in 2018, I wanted to give investors an overview of where we are at and what to expect as the trend evolves, because it is not going anywhere and will touch all aspects of this sector. For those that have shares of Netflix, Amazon and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), be warned that this space is anything by settled.
1) Hulu’s Cautionary Tale Can’t Be Overstated As mentioned above, the big three in this space are Netflix, Hulu and Amazon, but if you had to rank it entering 2017, Hulu would have slipped to third, maybe even further. Though now, the rankings are shaking up.
Hulu, when first created, set the model for what streaming TV could be. As it was a free service, it could only go so far, but with the pay model, we saw a clear evolution. Though it took until now for Hulu to be seen as an actual player.
